messages.content: Explain why Earth has seasons. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: Earth has seasons because its rotational axis is tilted about 23.5 degrees relative to the plane of its orbit around the Sun. As Earth travels along its orbit, this tilt causes different hemispheres to receive sunlight at varying angles and for different lengths of time throughout the year. When a hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it experiences more direct sunlight and longer days, producing summer, while the hemisphere tilted away gets less direct light and shorter days, producing winter.
